title: Minimize Max Distance to Gas Station
statement: Gas stations sit at sorted positions on a line. You may add k more stations at any real-valued positions. Return the smallest achievable value of the largest gap between neighbouring stations. Answers within 1e-5 are accepted.

large_tests.gen_code:
def gen():
    return [[i * 7 + (i * i) % 13 for i in range(2000)], 100000]

hints.1_question: If someone claims the largest gap can be at most D, how many extra stations would you need? How does that number change as D grows?
hints.2_nudge: Binary search D on real numbers. For a gap g you need ceil(g / D) - 1 extra stations so no piece exceeds D. Sum them and compare with k.
hints.3_big_hint: lo = 0, hi = largest gap. Repeat ~50-100 times: mid; need = sum(int(g / mid)); if need <= k: hi = mid else lo = mid. Return hi.

known_bugs.name: upper bound is the smallest gap
known_bugs.followup: With gaps 1 and 9 and one new station, can the answer be 1? What is the largest value the answer could ever be?

known_bugs.name: stops searching with a coarse tolerance
known_bugs.followup: How close must the answer be to the true value? What precision does your loop stop at?

known_bugs.name: halves the biggest gap repeatedly (greedy)
known_bugs.followup: With one gap of 10 and two new stations, what is the best result? Does halving the gap twice give it?

followups: Why can't a normal integer binary search be used here directly?
How would a max-heap greedy solution behave, and why is it slower?
